records.query: Need the patient's high-resolution esophageal manometry and videofluoroscopic swallow study reports, specifically UES relaxation and pharyngeal contraction parameters, plus details of previous dilation endpoints and symptom response, to confirm cricopharyngeal dysfunction as primary and rule out persistent distal structural obstruction.

Need the patient's cricopharyngeal muscle biopsy pathology report and prior barium esophagram with pharyngeal views documenting a cricopharyngeal bar, plus any neurologic or neuromuscular evaluation for UES dysfunction, to confirm cricopharyngeal hypertrophy as the primary cause and exclude alternative causes of impaired UES opening.
records.text:
Preoperative barium swallow imaging
Image Description: Showing obvious hypertrophy of the cricopharyngeal muscle. Thumbprint sign with cricopharyngeal bar was present on esophagram.

Histopathologic examination revealed:
- Nonnecrotizing granulomas and mononuclear inflammatory infiltrates in the endomysium
- Adipose tissue deposition
- Endomysial fibrosis
- Increased variation in muscle fiber size
- Increased internal nuclei
- Rare necrotic fibers
Special stains for acid-fast, fungal, and bacterial microorganisms were negative..

records.query: Need the high-resolution esophageal manometry report with UES resting and residual pressures plus pharyngeal contraction parameters, along with the videofluoroscopic swallow study and any neurologic/neuromuscular evaluation, to confirm impaired UES opening as the primary mechanism and exclude alternative causes.

Need serum ACE, calcium, and chest CT to evaluate for sarcoidosis/granulomatous myopathy given nonnecrotizing granulomas on cricopharyngeal biopsy, plus esophageal pH monitoring to exclude GERD as a contributing factor.
